deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are Grothendieck's 1953 notes on Hilbert tensor products. On the previous page he defined E ⊗^(2) F as the completion of the algebraic tensor product E⊗F for the inner product (x⊗y, x'⊗y') = (x,x')(y,y'). He showed that the products of orthonormal bases form an orthonormal basis, that ||x⊗y||_2 = ||x|| ||y||, and that the conjugate space of E⊗^(2)F is canonically Ē⊗^(2)F̄.

This page gives the basic example: identifying a Hilbert tensor product with a space of vector-valued L^2 functions. The top block is a crossed-out first attempt at the same statement.

Setup:
- M is a locally compact space with a positive (Radon) measure μ.
- L^2(μ) carries (φ,ψ) = ∫ φ ψ̄ dμ.
- For a Banach space E, L^2_E(μ) is the space of (suitably measurable) E-valued functions of square-integrable norm, with norm (9): ||f||_2 = (∫ ||f(t)||^2 dμ)^{1/2}. This makes it a Banach space; the reference to justify this is left blank.
- If E is Hilbert, the norm comes from the inner product (10): (f,g) = ∫ (f(t), g(t)) dμ(t), so L^2_E(μ) is a Hilbert space.

The map: the bilinear map (φ,a) ↦ φ·a from L^2 × E to L^2_E induces a linear map u ↦ ũ from L^2⊗E to L^2_E, with dense image.

Isometry: (φ·a, ψ·b) = (φ,ψ)(a,b), which is exactly the inner product of φ⊗a and ψ⊗b. By sesquilinearity, (ũ,ṽ) = (u,v) for all u,v in L^2⊗E. So the map is an isometric embedding of pre-Hilbert spaces with dense image. It therefore extends to an isomorphism from the completion L^2(μ)⊗^(2)E onto L^2_E(μ).

This is stated on the next page as Theorem 1, formula (11). The corollaries there are:
- l^2(I)⊗^(2)E = l^2_E(I);
- L^2(μ)⊗^(2)L^2(ν) = L^2(μ⊗ν).

Purpose: to build up the standard Hilbert-space facts needed before identifying Ē⊗^(2)F with the Hilbert–Schmidt operators (start of the next page). This is part of the general programme of comparing topological tensor products with spaces of operators and of vector-valued functions.
errors: Density of the image of L^2⊗E in L^2_E is asserted without proof. It requires the measurability convention (Bochner/strong measurability, or Bourbaki's μ-measurability) and density of step functions; the proof is not written.
The Banach-space completeness of L^2_E(μ) is left with an empty reference '( )' and no proof.
Formula (10) writes ⟨f(t), ḡ(t)⟩, mixing bilinear-pairing notation with conjugation; it is equivalent to the Hilbert inner product (f(t),g(t)). This is only a notational point.

ideas.what: Vector-valued L^2 space L^2_E(μ) for a Banach or Hilbert space E, with Hilbert structure when E is Hilbert
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 1955), discussion of L^1_E and L^p_E

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism L^2(μ) ⊗_2 E ≅ L^2_E(μ) via the dense isometric embedding φ⊗a ↦ φ·a
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert tensor product with L^2 equals vector-valued L^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Murray–von Neumann (1936), von Neumann (1939, infinite tensor products); standard textbook fact (e.g. Reed–Simon II.4)
ideas.where_published: Analogous L^1 statement L^1⊗^π E = L^1_E is in Produits tensoriels topologiques; the Hilbert version is likely mentioned there or in the Résumé, but unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard textbook identification of the Hilbert tensor product with vector-valued L^2, already known from Murray–von Neumann. Here it is written up as preparatory lecture-note material, with no novel construction or connection.
